    Transporting the distinguished basis vector along its own string #

    The self-evaluation of a Butler--Ringel detector rests on one elementary calculation: starting with the source-position basis vector of a literal string module and transporting its span along any prefix of the same word reaches the basis vector at the end of that prefix. Positive letters use the displayed-arrow image; inverse letters use its preimage.

    source
    theorem MagnitudeConjecture.BoundQuiver.StringWord.Word.not_exists_arrowStep_sourcePosition_of_prepend_negative_isString {k Q : Type u} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {R : RelationFamily k Q} (D : Word R) {y : Q} (a : D.source ⟶ y) (hstring : IsString R ((Quiver.Hom.toPath (negativeArrow a)).comp D.path)) :
    ¬∃ (j : D.PositionAt y), D.ArrowStep a D.sourcePosition j

    If the inverse of an outgoing arrow can be prefixed to a string, that arrow kills the string module's source-position basis vector.

    source
